title: Refactor button spacing tokens, chart legend variants, and table row auto-layout
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Summary:
We need to stabilize several Figma components that have grown inconsistent after last token migration: primary/secondary/ghost button spacing differs across variants, chart legend items render differently between compact and stacked variants, and table row auto-layout breaks on variable content heights. These issues are causing implementation drift and flaky visual regressions in product.

Goals:
- Consolidate spacing tokens used by buttons into a single semantic set (btn-pad-compact, btn-pad-default, btn-pad-wide) and update all button variants to reference them.
- Normalize chart legend components so that compact and stacked legend variants share a single base component with overrides for alignment and wrapping.
- Repair table row auto-layout constraints so rows stretch correctly when multi-line cells appear, and ensure selection/focus states remain aligned with cells.

Acceptance criteria:
- All button variants use the new semantic spacing tokens and render identically across primary/secondary/ghost states in mobile and desktop frames in Figma.
- Chart legend has a base component and two variant toggles (compact, stacked); QA checklist validates wrapping behavior at 320px, 480px, and 1024px widths.
- Table row components use consistent auto-layout rules: fixed cell padding based on tokens, vertical alignment centered, and no overlap when content grows; selection/highlight overlay aligns within grid.
- Updated Figma library published with clear changelog entries and a rollout note in Confluence for implementers.

Proposed steps:
1) Audit existing button, chart legend, and table components to map current token usage and variant differences (deliverable: audit spreadsheet).
2) Define semantic spacing tokens and update token aliases in the Figma Styles panel.
3) Create canonical base components for button, chart legend, and table-row; migrate existing variants to reference the base.
4) Run a small QA pass with two product pages (Dashboard table, Insights chart) to catch edge cases.
5) Publish library and announce rollout; include migration notes and code examples for engineers.

Risks / trade-offs:
- Renaming tokens will require engineers to update mappings; keep old token aliases for one release to avoid breaking integrations.
- Large-scale component edits may create noise in consumers' Figma files; aim for minimal rename surface and clearly document changes.
